name: usbcap-synth
experiment:
# USB packet capture. URB events become timestamped "usb" packets and a pcapng
# artifact (link type 220, usbmon) that Wireshark decodes natively.
#
# This example uses the plugin's SYNTHETIC source: a made-up HID mouse, a
# mass-storage stick and a CDC serial port being enumerated and used. Nothing
# is read from a bus. Real USB capture (Linux usbmon) has NOT been validated on
# this host: it needs root or a readable /sys/kernel/debug/usb/usbmon.
#
#   HWLAB_USBCAP_SYNTH=1 hwlab run --yes examples/usbcap-synth.yaml
#   hwlab usb analyze latest
#   hwlab usb analyze latest --device 1:5 --errors
#
# Real sources, instead of HWLAB_USBCAP_SYNTH:
#
#   # live, as root (or with debugfs mounted and readable); usbmon0 = every bus
#   sudo modprobe usbmon
#   hwlab devices                                  # usbcap/usbmon1 ...
#
#   # a usbmon text capture taken elsewhere (cat /sys/kernel/debug/usb/usbmon/1u > mon.txt)
#   HWLAB_USBCAP_SOURCES=lab=mon.txt hwlab run --yes examples/usbcap-synth.yaml   # device: lab
#
# USB payloads can contain keystrokes and secrets: snaplen limits what is kept
# (0 = headers only).
name: usbcap-synth
duration: 2s

devices:
  usb:
    plugin: usbcap
    device: synthetic
    speed: 1          # offline sources only: replay speed factor
    snaplen: 256

steps:
  - {name: info, at: 100ms, device: usb, call: USBPacketCapture.info}

clock.source: synthetic generator timeline, paced on the host clock
clock.note: synthetic data: the timing is made up and says nothing about any bus
